items.title: AI Company Employees Petition US Government For Regulation - Engadget
items.summary: AI company employees petition US government for regulation. A thousand workers from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and more have signed the letter. A collection of employees at major artificial intelligence firms has created a petition asking for the federal government to help "deliberately pace" the development of the transformative technology. *Bloomberg* reports that more than 1,100 workers from companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and more signed the missive. "We request that the US government support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development," the petition states. The letter claims there is "a real risk" of AI "understand or control". Reaching out to a federal government that has taken a haphazard approach to understanding and regulating AI, as well as a belligerent attitude toward international collaboration, seems like a gesture they must know is futile. But perhaps the growing number of incidents where agentic AI causes major security issues is enough to spark real action.

items.title: Stronger AI Safety Requires Peeking Inside the 'Black Box' - Dark Reading
items.summary: Adding security to AI often treats the large language model (LLM) or AI system as a black box, focusing on analyzing the tokenized inputs and outputs but not what goes on inside the model. A group of offensive-security researchers hopes to change that, presenting at the Black Hat USA 2026 in August a model-agnostic approach to activation analysis with standardized rules for processing activation events. The goal is to create an open system of identified cognitive elements and rules that detect specific types of safety events, similar to Snort or YARA rulesets, says Yisroel Mirsky, an assistant professor and head of the Offensive AI Research Lab at Ben-Gurion University of The Negev. Analyzing the tokenized input to or output of a model is similar to antivirus scanning and heuristics — it's fast and catches a wide variety of attacks, raising the bar for attackers, but defense in depth needs more layers, says Mirsky.

items.title: LLM Evaluation: Metrics, Methods, and Best Practices
items.summary:
Your retrieval-augmented generation pipeline introduces evaluation challenges beyond what model-level metrics capture. You need to assess both the retrieval component and the end-to-end generation quality separately.

### Metrics for retrieval quality

You evaluate your retrieval component by measuring whether it surfaces the right documents for a given query. Standard information retrieval metrics apply here: [...] Evaluate retrieval and generation separately. For retrieval, measure Precision@K, Recall@K, MRR, and nDCG against labeled relevance judgments. For end-to-end quality, frameworks like RAGAS score faithfulness (does the answer stay true to retrieved context?), answer relevance, and context relevance. Watch for context poisoning, where retrieved errors get reproduced, and context distraction, where irrelevant documents drown out what matters.

Aron Schuhmann [...] TruLens provides feedback functions that measure faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance, giving you granular insight into where your retrieval and generation components succeed or fail. You can trace how each piece of retrieved context influenced the final output and build custom feedback functions for domain-specific evaluation criteria.

This paper presents an enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) chatbot framework for efficient retrieval and interpretation of complex technical documentation in the printed circuit board (PCB) manufacturing domain. Two RAG architectures, LongRAG and GraphRAG, are systematically evaluated using domain-specific equipment manuals. Quantitative results show that LongRAG achieves higher answer relevancy, while GraphRAG produces more faithful responses. items.title: TeaRAG: A Token-Efficient Agentic Retrieval-Augmented ...
items.summary:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) utilizes external knowledge to augment Large Language Models’ (LLMs) reliability.
For flexibility, agentic RAG employs autonomous, multi-round retrieval and reasoning to resolve queries.
Although recent agentic RAG has improved via reinforcement learning, they often incur substantial token overhead from search and reasoning. This trade-off prioritizes accuracy over efficiency. [...] One-turn generation prepares all the required information and utilize the LLM in a single pass to generate the final answer.
The methods in this category are as follows:

Zero-shot: This method uses the LLM to generate answers without retrieving relevant information.

RAG (Lewis et al., 2020): This is the standard RAG method that uses semantic retrieval to search for relevant text chunks from the corpus, which are then input as evidence to the LLM to directly generate answers. [...] Large Language Models (LLMs) have made substantial progress through learning from massive pre‑training corpora.
Nevertheless, statistical inaccuracies in linguistic distribution modeling during pre‑training can lead to hallucination generation (Kalai et al., 2025).
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is an effective technique that mitigates hallucinations in LLMs by incorporating external retrieval information (Gao et al., 2023; Lyu et al., 2025a).

items.title: MLTut - How does RAG actually work? Let me break it down...
items.summary:
## MLTut's Post

### MLTut

9h  ·

How does RAG actually work? Let me break it down in simple words-

RAG = Retrieval-Augmented Generation.

It just means the LLM doesn't answer from its own memory, it first goes and fetches the relevant info, then answers using that info.

This is the flow-

1. Load your documents (PDFs, txt, websites, whatever)

2. Split them into small chunks

3. Convert those chunks into embeddings and store them in a vector DB (FAISS, Chroma, Pinecone) [...] 4. When user asks a question, find the most relevant chunks using similarity search

5. Give those chunks + the question to the LLM

6. LLM generates a grounded answer, no hallucination

That's it. Retrieval brings the knowledge, generation brings the language. Together they give you accurate, up-to-date answers even on your own private data.

If you want to build this yourself, I made a complete video on building a local RAG app-

items.summary: Despite American export controls designed to cut Huawei off from the world's most advanced semiconductor technology, China's largest technology company is poised to post a 60% jump in chip revenue this year — a far cry from the death blow the Biden administration had hoped the restrictions would deliver. Following export controls implemented in 2023, China directed its state agencies to purchase hardware, chips, mobile devices and software from Huawei while also pouring over $1 billion in government grants into the company. "The export controls announced in the two rules today restrict the PRC’s ability to obtain advanced computing chips, develop and maintain supercomputers, and manufacture advanced semiconductors," the U.S. Department of Commerce wrote in a statement at the time. Even so, the investments have coincided with an important milestone by 2026: the emergence of the Ascend 910B chip — a jump in China’s cutting-edge technology designed to compete with Nvidia's chips.

items.title: China’s Domestic DUV Push Puts ASML’s Export-Control Advantage on Trial - EU Today
items.summary: # China’s Domestic DUV Push Puts ASML’s Export-Control Advantage on Trial. #### Reported production of China’s first home-grown immersion lithography machines does not erase ASML’s technical lead. It does show how controls designed to deny advanced tools can accelerate the creation of a rival supply chain. China has reportedly begun manufacturing domestically developed immersion deep-ultraviolet lithography systems, prompting a sharp fall in European semiconductor-equipment shares and turning a long-running industrial ambition into an immediate commercial question for ASML. Reuters reported, citing an investigation by The Information, that about five of the Chinese machines are expected to be produced in 2026 and roughly 20 next year. Nor is the new machine described as an equal substitute for ASML’s current equipment. The reported Chinese system still lags in performance and reliability and needs further testing before it can be regarded as ready for mass production. Those caveats explain why the development is not the sudden collapse of Europe’s most important technology monopoly.

items.title: Staff warned of major security risks from giving UAE new tech access. The White House went ahead anyway. - POLITICO Pro
items.summary: Commerce Department staffers recommended against loosening export restrictions on the Gulf ally in previously unreported warnings, arguing it could make it easier for China to get its hands on sensitive American technology. **ENERGYWIRE |** The Trump administration ignored warnings from career staff at the Commerce Department when it granted the United Arab Emirates sweeping access to advanced American semiconductors and other technology, according to three former officials with knowledge of the reports and two other people familiar with the matter. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security announced on July 10 that it was loosening restrictions on sensitive tech exports to the UAE, a key ally in the war in the Middle East whose leaders pledged last year to invest more than $1 trillion in the U.S. over the coming decade. According to one of the people familiar and two former officials, the announcement surprised staff inside the agency, which is tasked with securing American tech from adversaries and criminals.
